title: Back Behind the Wheel
summary:
Back Behind the Wheel
Memorial Day weekend in the United States signifies to most the unofficial start to the summer season. For those in the gasoline and tanker markets, this weekend symbolizes the kick-off to a period of high demand for petroleum products. The Automobile Association of America tracks the number of travelers driving at least 50 miles from home.

children.title: Premium
children.summary: Regular Current Price Premium Current Price Regular The chart highlights price levels on previous Memorial Day weekends, current prices are approximately 40% less than price levels a year ago, but within the five-year historical range. Lower prices can be seen as a relief for American vacationers, but may have different consequences for others in the oil market.

children.title: Downward Demand
children.summary: With the health of the overall economy starkly different from a year ago, gasoline demand is about 4% lower year-on-year. On a practical basis demand is even less when adjusted for hydrocarbon content due to ethanol mandates.

children.summary: 2008 3-2-1 Crack Spread 2009 3-2-1 Crack Spread Refining margins are lower as compared to a year ago and the price strength favors gasoline rather than diesel. Since the crude oil freight component is adding less pressure to the bottom line, refiners may be tempted to ramp up runs seeking higher gasoline output.
